CEP-2026-10-001.stem: A business unit deploys an AI tool to recommend customer eligibility decisions. The tool has been added to the enterprise risk register, and the vendor provides an accuracy certificate. What further measure is MOST important?
options: Review vendor certifications, document intended data inputs and require a qualified reviewer to approve eligibility exceptions after launch.
Map privacy and legal obligations for the workflow and assign a human appeals route, relying on the vendor’s technical performance tests for routine outcomes.
Evaluate legal, operational, privacy, and decision risks; establish permitted inputs and meaningful human review of outputs.
Pilot the customer-decision system with restricted inputs and management oversight, using later complaint trends as the principal fairness measure.
CEP-2026-10-001.explanation: The article explicitly treats AI as an independent risk requiring usage rules, information protection, and critical human validation. Recording the tool in a risk matrix or relying on supplier certification is not equivalent to controls over decisions.
CEP-2026-10-001.source: CEP Magazine, 2026-10, printed p. 26: Regulating AI in our compliance program

CEP-2026-11-001.article: Beyond the investigation: The strategic value of mediation
CEP-2026-11-001.stem: An employee reports possible retaliation after raising a compliance concern. During intake, the investigator notices inconsistencies in the sequence of events. What interviewing technique is MOST likely to improve procedural fairness and evidence quality?
options: Begin with open questions about the alleged retaliation, then use management documents to resolve contradictory dates before asking for a complete narrative.
Invite a chronological account and explore inconsistencies immediately as they appear, recording agreed details before moving on.
Ask the interviewee to review a draft timeline of material events, then use neutral questions to fill gaps and correct the record.
Invite an uninterrupted chronological narrative, listen actively, and then clarify inconsistencies through neutral, focused questions.
CEP-2026-11-001.explanation: The article connects procedural fairness and active listening with better evidence. It specifically contrasts an early challenge to perceived inconsistencies with allowing a chronological narrative before clarification.
CEP-2026-11-001.source: CEP Magazine, 2026-11, printed p. 20: Beyond the investigation: The strategic value of mediation
